_meta.description: Curated list of London new-build sources that have actually synced successfully at least once, plus (as of 2026-08) two explicitly-tagged third-party aggregator sources (source_type: "aggregator") and several general estate-agent sources (source_type: "estate-agent": Winkworth, Benhams London, Hamptons, Knight Frank, Renowned Homes — most tagged trustAsNewBuild since their page/section is already new-build-curated by the site itself; Winkworth alone still runs its own text-based new-build filter). Direct-developer entries (source_type absent, the default) are still primary — see rules below.
_meta.usage: Import into the Home Finder project. Build one adapter per entry keyed by id. The sync job must filter out auction and retirement stock, and must NEVER substitute placeholder/mock data when a fetch fails - return empty and record the failure in sync_status.
rules: Every listing's source label must be the real developer/aggregator/estate-agent name from this file.
No fabricated listings, prices, areas, postcodes, images, or sources.
If an adapter fails or is blocked, return empty and log to sync_status - do not invent data.

source_type: "aggregator" entries (1newhomes, Benhams) are real third-party listing sites, not developers' own sites — kept clearly labelled and lower-priority. Their listings are deduped against direct-developer listings before being stored (see lib/adapters/dedupe.ts) — a direct-developer listing always wins; an aggregator listing is only kept when it isn't already covered by a direct source.

source_type: "estate-agent" is a general estate agent, not a new-build specialist by nature — its adapter, by default, discards any listing without a genuine new-build signal (own text, or a structured field) before it's ever stored, the opposite default from every other source here (see hasExplicitNewBuildSignal in lib/adapters/newBuildDetection.ts). Treated the same as an aggregator for phase-ordering/dedupe (see isSecondPhaseSource in lib/developers.ts).

trustAsNewBuild: true (Winkworth, Benhams London, Hamptons, Knight Frank, Renowned Homes) bypasses that default entirely for a source whose page/section is already curated as new-build-only by the site itself — every listing the adapter collects is kept and stored as isNewBuild: true, no per-listing filtering (see trustsAsNewBuild in lib/developers.ts).

2026-08: cross-source dedup (lib/adapters/dedupe.ts) was extended from "aggregator vs direct developers only" to every second-phase source against every other active listing — direct developers still always win; among second-phase sources, whichever is registered (and therefore synced) first in this array wins a duplicate. This is why benhams-london is listed AFTER benhams above (both are the same agency's own catalog, reached via different pages, and heavily overlap).

2026-08: pruned to exactly the sources that have ever synced successfully (status ok, real listings, a real last-success timestamp) — every source that had never once produced a real listing (status error/blocked, 0 listings, last success 'Never') was permanently removed from this file, the adapters registry, and Supabase (sync_status/listings rows for a source_id no longer in this file are deleted by lib/db.ts's pruneUnknownSources, which runs at the start of every sync). A future candidate developer should only be re-added here once it has a working, verified adapter — not spec-listed speculatively.

fields.priority: 1 = build first (high volume / clean site), 4 = build last, 5 = aggregator/estate-agent (lower priority than any direct developer)
fields.off_portal_value: how likely crawling this source catches for-sale stock not on Rightmove/Zoopla
fields.tenures: tenure types this developer typically sells
fields.source_type: "aggregator" for third-party listing sites, "estate-agent" for a general estate agent; absent/default means a direct developer source
fields.trustAsNewBuild: true bypasses an estate-agent source's own new-build discard filter entirely — every listing is kept and stored as new-build; absent/default means the source's own filter (if any) still applies

developers.name: Redrow
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/redrow.ts) — same underlying platform as Barratt London (now the same corporate group, Barratt Redrow): GET /api/search/devplots?brandCodes=red returns every Redrow development nationwide (needs London postcode filtering — confirmed live, only 4 of 103 are genuinely London-area), each development's own page server-renders real plot cards in the identical markup Barratt's adapter already parses.

developers.name: Bellway London
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/bellwayLondon.ts) — Bellway has no single London hub; the adapter scans several regional division pages and keeps only developments whose own published address says London/Greater London. listings_url is the regions index, not scraped directly.

developers.name: Vistry / Countryside Partnerships
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/countryside.ts) — the search-results?location=london URL requested 2026-08 is still disallowed by robots.txt (`Disallow: /*?` blocks every query-string URL on this domain, confirmed live again), so per user decision (2026-08) this instead uses a real, public, robots.txt-compliant data feed found via the site's own sitemap: /data/developments/csv (42 developments nationwide, one row per development). London filtering trusts the feed's own url region-slug (`/developments/london/...`), which is more precise than a postcode-area heuristic here — it excludes two developments (South Oxhey Central WD19, Ashmere/Ebbsfleet DA10) that a bare postcode check would wrongly include.

developers.name: Berkeley Group
developers.notes: Unified brand since March 2026 (was St George/St James/St Edward/St William/St Joseph/Berkeley Homes)

developers.name: L&Q
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/lqHomes.ts) — uses the site's own wp-json/custom/developments + development/{id}/properties JSON endpoints, captured from this exact search URL. listings_url intentionally fixed, not auto-discovered.

developers.name: 1newhomes
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/oneNewHomes.ts) — third-party London new-homes aggregator, ~1,570 developments across ~79 pages (path-based pagination: /new-homes/page-2, /new-homes/page-3, ... — no query string, so robots.txt's `Disallow: /new-homes/*?` doesn't apply). Deduped against direct-developer listings before storage — see _meta.rules.

developers.name: Benhams
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/benhams.ts) — third-party London (and a little Home Counties) new-homes aggregator, ~284 developments loaded 32 at a time via a real "Load more" button (GET /new-homes?...&page=N, no robots.txt conflict). Deduped against direct-developer listings before storage — see _meta.rules.

developers.name: Benhams London
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/benhamsLondon.ts) — a SEPARATE page from the existing benhams (/new-homes/) entry above, not a duplicate of it: benhams.com's dedicated London new-build campaign hub, ~96 development campaigns loaded 16 at a time via a real "Load more" button (POST /api/v1/campaign/listing/, a genuine JSON endpoint). No price on the list cards themselves — one extra real fetch per campaign's own detail page for its published "from £X" figure; no bedroom count ever published. trustAsNewBuild set (this hub is Benhams' own dedicated new-build page by construction). Registered AFTER the existing benhams entry so that source wins on the heavy overlap explicitly expected between the two Benhams pages — see lib/adapters/dedupe.ts.

developers.name: Winkworth
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/winkworth.ts) — general London estate agent, added 2026-08 as an explicit test of this app's resale-filtering approach. Uses Winkworth's own dedicated new-homes section (not the general for-sale search) — the section is already curated as new-build by the site itself, so trustAsNewBuild is set: the adapter's own hasExplicitNewBuildSignal discard filter is bypassed entirely (it was excluding real new-build listings whose text just didn't happen to use one of the checked phrases, e.g. off-plan retirement apartments described only as 'by award-winning builder... will be decorated') — every listing collected here is kept and stored as isNewBuild: true. listings_url is fixed at priceto=500000 (14 results at time of writing; removing the cap gives 53 across the same section — a deliberate choice left to whoever configures this entry, not auto-widened). robots.txt disallows ClaudeBot by name (Cloudflare-managed, confirmed live 2026-08, same shape of conflict as ecoworld-london's) — proceeding here was an explicit, informed user override, not an oversight; /api/ still respected (this adapter only ever fetches the public search-results HTML page). Deep-paginated via the site's own embedded JSON feed (data-dc-search-results-list attribute, ?page=N). Deduped against direct-developer listings before storage — see _meta.rules.

developers.name: Hamptons
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/hamptons.ts) — general London estate agent, Hamptons' own "new homes" tag capped at £450,000. No network-json listings feed (checked live — only analytics/chat traffic); real data comes from a server-rendered CollectionPage/OfferCatalog JSON-LD block (extractionMethod: json-ld), path-paginated (/page-2, /page-3, ...), 51 offers / 5 pages at time of writing. No image on the list feed itself — one extra real fetch per listing for its detail page's og:image and fuller description (used for tenure text). trustAsNewBuild set (this is Hamptons' own new-homes tag). Deduped against every other active listing before storage — see lib/adapters/dedupe.ts.

developers.name: Knight Frank
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/knightFrank.ts) — general London estate agent, filtered to Knight Frank's own "New Build"/"New Development"/"New Homes" feature tags (ids 299,300,16915) and capped at £500,000. Real network-json feed (api-v2.web.prd-knightfrank.com/properties/search, captured live via the page's own network response — a bare fetch to it returns 401, so it's read from the real page load, not replayed standalone), full per-property data including real image URLs, no extra per-listing fetch needed. 10 results at time of writing, all fit in one response (Offset/Limit/Total-driven "Load More" pagination implemented for when that changes). trustAsNewBuild set (already scoped to Knight Frank's own new-build feature tags). Deduped against every other active listing before storage — see lib/adapters/dedupe.ts.

developers.name: Renowned Homes
developers.notes: Dedicated adapter (lib/adapters/renownedHomes.ts) — new-homes estate agent/aggregator (lists real developer names per card — Taylor Wimpey, EcoWorld, Berkeley, ...), capped at £450,000. No network-json feed (checked live — only Next.js RSC prefetch traffic); real data comes from server-rendered .dev_card HTML, query-string paginated (?page=N), ~13 pages at time of writing. Postcode not on the list card — one extra real fetch per listing for its detail page's own <meta name="description"> text, which states it directly. trustAsNewBuild set (every developer shown here sells new-build only). Heavy overlap with direct developers expected and handled — deduped against every other active listing before storage, see lib/adapters/dedupe.ts.
